title: Graph-normalized chart models and independent compactifications
statement:
Let $R$ be a finite commutative torsion ring. Let $U,V,Y$ be Noetherian schemes, meaning schemes with finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings, and let $e:U\to V$ be separated etale of finite type and $f:V\to Y$ separated of finite type. Put $g=fe$ and choose compactifications $c_e,c_f,c_g$ with Noetherian middle schemes [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Work in the ordinary constant-$R$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $h=e,f,g$ write $F_{h,R}^{c_h}=Rr_{h*,R}Dj_{h!,R}$ for the chosen compact-support candidate [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and put $E_R=De_{\Sigma!,R}$ for exact etale sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension].
The canonical family $c_{v,c}:F_{v,R}^c\xrightarrow{\sim}Dv_{\Sigma!,R}$ of [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization], as $v$ ranges over separated finite-type etale maps of Noetherian schemes, furnishes a graph-normalized datum of [def-sp-etale-compact-support-normalization]. In particular it admits sheaf maps $a_{v,c}:v_{\Sigma!}\to r_*j_!$ whose composite to $v_*$ is graph extension and whose degreewise descent followed by the right-derived unit is $c_{v,c}^{-1}$; it has the specified proper/open base-change, identity, composition, refinement and sum/evaluation counit normalizations of that datum.
On $D^+(U_{et},R)$ let $\alpha_R:F_{f,R}^{c_f}F_{e,R}^{c_e}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g,R}^{c_g}$ be canonical compact-support composition [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Then
$$\lambda_R=\alpha_R\circ F_{f,R}^{c_f}(c_{e,c_e}^{-1}):F_{f,R}^{c_f}E_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g,R}^{c_g}$$
is exactly the restricted-closure comparison of [def-sp-etale-adjoint-chart-comparison] for the displayed datum. For any second triple of Noetherian compactifications, let $\rho_{h,R}:F_{h,R}^{c_h}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h,R}^{c'_h}$ be comparison through any common refinement. The actual maps satisfy
$$c_{e,c'_e}\circ\rho_{e,R}=c_{e,c_e},\qquad \lambda'_R\circ(\rho_{f,R}E_R)=\rho_{g,R}\circ\lambda_R.$$
These identities are independent of the chosen common refinement and satisfy its identity and cocycle laws.
